description_full: EMCOR Group, Inc. provides electrical and mechanical construction and facilities, building, and industrial services in the United States and the United Kingdom. It offers design, integration, installation, startup, operation, and maintenance services related to power transmission, distribution, and generation systems; energy solutions; premises electrical and lighting systems; process instrumentation; low-voltage systems; voice and data communications systems; roadway and transit lighting, signaling, and fiber optic lines; computerized traffic control systems, and signal and communication equipment; heating, ventilation, air conditioning, refrigeration, and geothermal solutions; clean-room process ventilation systems; fire protection and suppression systems; plumbing, process, and piping systems; control and filtration systems; water and wastewater treatment systems; central plant heating and cooling systems; crane and rigging; millwright; and steel fabrication, erection, and welding services. The company also provides site-based operations and maintenance; facility management and maintenance; energy retrofit; military base operations support; indoor air quality; floor care and janitorial; landscaping, lot sweeping, and snow removal; vendor management and call center; installation and support for building systems; program development, management, and maintenance for energy systems; technical consulting and diagnostic; infrastructure and building projects; modification and retrofit projects; and reception, security, and catering services. In addition, it offers refinery turnaround planning and engineering; welding; overhaul and maintenance; technical; instrumentation, controls, and electrical; electrical panel design, fabrication, and installation; on-site repair and maintenance; and renewable energy services, as well as design, manufacturing, repair, and hydro blast cleaning services. The company was incorporated in 1987 and is headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut.

financial_summary: EMCOR Group, Inc. is a large-cap industrials business with a $26.6B market cap on $17.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +15% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 37% against a 10% cost of capital — a 27-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 15% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.02× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 10% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.92x).
It accounts for 0.4% of sector revenue and 0.4% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+30.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 544 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 26% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 26% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 36% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 43% and a beta of 1.08, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $287.9M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash, 26% in the 2022 bear market and 67% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $579 (margin of safety -5%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 26%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $449 to $765 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 17.6 vs 23.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 44% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 4.5% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $907 on average, 49% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 37% clears the cost of capital of 10.1% by 27pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.77).
It runs a 15% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.02x.
ROE of 35% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $545.5M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.3, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 15.3% over 3 years, 14.1% over 5 years and 9.7% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 9.4% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.19 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 78% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 14%.
Capex runs 1.7x depreciation (0.7% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 15.9% on average.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.7%), and institutions hold 98%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 5 sales over the past year, net $6.2M sold.
It returns 2.4% a year to shareholders (2.2% in buybacks and 0.3% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 14 consecutive years, raising it 20.6% a year over the last five.
people: With about 44,000 employees, each generates about $386K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median, and productivity has risen 8.3% a year.
That works out to $27K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $10.9M (28x revenue per employee).
